q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is 2026-08-13. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings would typically be released in late August or early September 2026 (NVIDIA typically reports quarterly earnings ~3-4 weeks after quarter end). Time remaining: approximately 2-3 weeks.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has explicitly guided for Q2 FY2027 revenue of **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.18B to $92.82B), released on 2026-05-20.

This guidance is the most concrete information available. The company has already provided official forward guidance, and we're now in the window where this guidance should be substantially firmed up (only weeks from actual reporting). Companies rarely dramatically revise official guidance between release and actual earnings, though modest adjustments are possible.

The analyst consensus estimate of $91.8 billion sits slightly above the midpoint of NVIDIA's guidance range ($91.0B), suggesting modest outperformance expectations but still well-aligned with management's guidance.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro deterioration**: If economic conditions weakened sharply or enterprise AI spending decelerated
- **Supply chain disruptions**: Unexpected fab or supply chain issues
- **China revenue headwinds**: Further tightening of export restrictions (the guidance already assumes zero China Data Center revenue)
- **Customer pushback/inventory corrections**: If key customers reduced orders unexpectedly
- **Conservative bias in guidance**: Companies sometimes guide conservatively to beat—though NVIDIA's track record shows confidence in their numbers

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Demand exceeds expectations**: Continued strong enterprise and cloud AI spending acceleration
- **Upside on existing guidance**: The ±2% range suggests management confidence; beating by $0.8B-$1.8B (0.9-2% above midpoint) is within normal operating variance
- **Inventory builds ahead of supply**: Customers may front-load orders expecting supply constraints
- **Better-than-expected mix**: Higher-margin products in the revenue mix
- **Positive surprises in cloud capex**: Major hyperscalers announcing larger AI infrastructure spending

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Q1 FY2027 actual revenue**: $81.6 billion (record, +85% YoY)
- **Q1 FY2027 data center growth**: +92% YoY
- **Q2 FY2027 official guidance**: $91.0B ± 2% ($89.18B–$92.82B)
- **Analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027**: $91.8 billion

The sequential growth from Q1 ($81.6B) to Q2 guided midpoint ($91.0B) is approximately +11.5%, which is substantial but plausible given the strong momentum and peak demand cycle for AI chips.

NVIDIA's recent earnings have shown the company beating guidance moderately—for instance, Q1 actual was at the higher end of their range. However, the forward guidance for Q2 appears to already embed confidence about demand.

## Reasoning on the range

The question asks for "forward guidance" which NVIDIA has already provided: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**. The resolution likely refers to what management will actually state in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release (which hasn't occurred yet, but the forward guidance has been issued).

The given range is 99.5B–115.5B (lower bound open, upper bound open). This is notably *above* NVIDIA's official guidance of $89.18B–$92.82B. This wider range suggests either:
1. The question anticipates NVIDIA may revise upward materially when they report Q2 results
2. The range is deliberately conservative to cover tail scenarios

Given we're only 2-3 weeks from earnings and guidance was just issued in May, a major upward revision to guidance would be unusual unless there's been a significant positive development. However, NVIDIA's strong momentum and track record of beating could support the higher range.

**My estimate**: I expect the actual Q2 FY2027 guidance to be within or very close to the already-announced $89.18B–$92.82B range, likely clustering around $90.5B–$92.5B. I assign meaningful but lower probability to material upside revisions (toward 95B+) given the recent guidance was firm.

NVIDIA has provided strong forward guidance for its second quarter of fiscal year 2027, expecting revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance, released on May 20, 2026, does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), driven by a 92% year-over-year increase in data center revenue [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report). Analysts' consensus revenue estimate for Q2 FY2027 is $91.8 billion [tickerleague.com](https://tickerleague.com/companies/NVDA/estimates).
